varies: 最初の質問は毎回変わります。
origNote: ロールカードはBabel Flightのオリジナルです(進め方・時間は本番と同じ。本番は職種ごとの試験です)。
markNote: 採点は本番のグレードとは違う、自分でつける目安です。
voiceNote: 対話者(患者や家族の役)の英語は、この端末の音声で読み上げます。医師・看護師になったつもりで答えよう。
sumNote: 本番は言葉の4観点と、臨床コミュニケーションの5観点で評価されます。70%をこえたら手ごたえあり。
againNote: 最初の質問は変わります
flow: ウォームアップ ・ 仕事についての質問(採点なし)
ロールプレイ1 ・ ロールカードを3分読む → 患者・家族役との会話(約5分)
ロールプレイ2 ・ 同じ流れ

open.t: Hello. My name is {ex}, and I'll be your interlocutor today. Can you tell me your name and your profession, please?
Thank you. Before we start the role-plays, I'd like to ask you a little about your work.

close.t: Thank you. That's the end of the speaking test.

points: 発音・強勢・リズムで伝わる
自然な速さ、不要な間を作らない
専門用語を患者向けに言いかえる
正確で多様な表現
あいさつ・共感・敬意
不安や考えを引き出して受けとめる
話の流れを示す(First, I'd like to …)
開いた質問 → 閉じた質問
少しずつ伝えて理解を確認する

roles.title: Role-play 1 (Medicine)
lines: Patient: a 45-year-old office worker who has come about headaches.
task: Find out more about the headaches (how long, when, how bad).
Ask about work, screen time, sleep and stress.
Reassure the patient that serious causes are unlikely.
Advise on lifestyle changes (regular breaks, water, sleep).
Explain when to come back.

roles.title: Role-play 2 (Medicine)
lines: Relative: the parent of a 9-year-old child with appendicitis. The child needs an operation today.
task: Explain the diagnosis in simple language.
Explain why an operation is needed today.
Respond to the parent's worries about the operation.
Explain what will happen next.
Check understanding and invite questions.

steps.t: Now let's start the first role-play. Here is your card. You have three minutes to prepare.

steps.label: ロールカードを読む(3分・メモOK)

steps.t: Are you ready? I'll start.
Hello, doctor. I've been getting these headaches for about three weeks now, and I'm getting a bit worried.

steps.cue: 頭痛についてくわしく聞く(いつ・どのくらい)

steps.t: They usually start in the afternoon, at work. Maybe a six. It feels like a tight band around my head.

steps.cue: 仕事・画面を見る時間・睡眠・ストレスをたずねる

steps.t: I'm on the computer most of the day, and I've been working late because of a big project. I only sleep about five hours.

steps.cue: 安心させる(重い病気の可能性は低い)

steps.t: That's a relief. But what can I do about them?

steps.cue: 生活の改善をアドバイス(休憩・水分・睡眠)

steps.t: OK, I'll try that. Should I come back?

steps.cue: いつ再受診すべきか説明する

steps.t: Thank you. That's the end of the first role-play.
Now let's start the second role-play. Here is your card. You have three minutes to prepare.

steps.label: ロールカードを読む(3分・メモOK)

steps.t: Are you ready? I'll start.
Doctor, what's wrong with my son? He's in so much pain.

steps.cue: 診断をわかりやすく説明する(虫垂炎)

steps.t: Does he really need an operation? Can't you give him medicine?

steps.cue: 今日手術が必要な理由を説明する

steps.t: I'm scared. He's never had an operation before.

steps.cue: 不安に寄りそう(よくある手術・安全性)

steps.t: What happens now?

steps.cue: 次の流れを説明する(麻酔科医・手術時間・回復)

steps.t: OK... I think I understand.

steps.cue: 理解を確認し、質問をうながす

steps.t: Thank you. That's the end of the second role-play.

r1_1.q: Hello, doctor. I've been getting these headaches for about three weeks now, and I'm getting a bit worried.
r1_1.ja: 頭痛についてくわしく聞く(いつ・どのくらい)
model: I'm sorry to hear that. Let's see if we can find out what's causing them. Can you tell me when the headaches usually start, and how bad they are on a scale of one to ten?
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_2.q: They usually start in the afternoon, at work. Maybe a six. It feels like a tight band around my head.
r1_2.ja: 仕事・画面を見る時間・睡眠・ストレスをたずねる
model: Thank you, that's helpful. Could you tell me a bit about your work? For example, how many hours a day do you spend in front of a computer, and how have you been sleeping recently?
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_3.q: I'm on the computer most of the day, and I've been working late because of a big project. I only sleep about five hours.
r1_3.ja: 安心させる(重い病気の可能性は低い)
model: I see. From what you've told me, these sound like tension headaches. They're very common and usually not caused by anything serious, so please try not to worry too much.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_4.q: That's a relief. But what can I do about them?
r1_4.ja: 生活の改善をアドバイス(休憩・水分・睡眠)
model: There are a few things that really help. Try to take a short break from the screen every hour, drink plenty of water, and aim for at least seven hours of sleep. Gentle neck stretches can also help.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_5.q: OK, I'll try that. Should I come back?
r1_5.ja: いつ再受診すべきか説明する
model: Yes, if the headaches don't improve in two weeks, or if you notice anything unusual, like problems with your vision or very sudden, severe pain, please come back straight away. Does that sound all right?
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_1.q: Doctor, what's wrong with my son? He's in so much pain.
r2_1.ja: 診断をわかりやすく説明する(虫垂炎)
model: I understand this is very worrying. Your son has appendicitis. That means his appendix, a small part of the bowel, has become inflamed and painful.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_2.q: Does he really need an operation? Can't you give him medicine?
r2_2.ja: 今日手術が必要な理由を説明する
model: That's a very good question. In his case, the appendix is badly swollen, and if we wait, it could burst and cause a serious infection. So the safest option is to remove it today.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_3.q: I'm scared. He's never had an operation before.
r2_3.ja: 不安に寄りそう(よくある手術・安全性)
model: It's completely natural to feel that way. This is one of the most common operations for children, and our team does it very often. He'll be asleep the whole time, so he won't feel any pain.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_4.ja: 次の流れを説明する(麻酔科医・手術時間・回復)
model: The anaesthetist will come to see you both shortly. The operation itself usually takes about an hour, and most children can go home after one or two days.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_5.ja: 理解を確認し、質問をうながす
model: Thank you for listening. Just to check, could you tell me in your own words why he needs the operation today? And please ask me anything you're unsure about.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

roles.title: Role-play 1 (Nursing)
lines: Patient: a 68-year-old man, one day after knee surgery, who does not want to get out of bed.
task: Find out why the patient does not want to walk.
Acknowledge his pain and fear.
Explain why walking soon after surgery is important.
Explain how you will help him walk safely.
Agree on a plan.

roles.title: Role-play 2 (Nursing)
lines: Patient: a 30-year-old woman going home today after minor surgery on her hand.
task: Explain how to look after the wound.
Explain the signs of infection.
Give advice about pain relief.
Explain when the stitches will be removed.
Check understanding.

steps.t: Now let's start the first role-play. Here is your card. You have three minutes to prepare.

steps.label: ロールカードを読む(3分・メモOK)

steps.t: Are you ready? I'll start.
Nurse, I'm not getting up today. My knee hurts too much.

steps.cue: 歩きたくない理由をたずねる

steps.t: Well, both. I'm afraid I'll fall and damage the new knee.

steps.cue: 痛みと不安を受けとめる

steps.t: So why can't I just stay in bed for a few days?

steps.cue: 早く歩くことの大切さを説明する(血栓・回復)

steps.t: But what if I fall?

steps.cue: 安全に歩くための支えを説明する(痛み止め・歩行器・付き添い)

steps.t: Hmm, OK. Maybe I can try.

steps.cue: 計画に合意する(30分後に)

steps.t: Thank you. That's the end of the first role-play.
Now let's start the second role-play. Here is your card. You have three minutes to prepare.

steps.label: ロールカードを読む(3分・メモOK)

steps.t: Are you ready? I'll start.
So I can go home now? What do I need to do with this bandage?

steps.cue: 傷の手当ての方法を説明する(乾かす)

steps.t: What if something goes wrong?

steps.cue: 感染のサインを説明する

steps.t: It's starting to hurt a little.

steps.cue: 痛み止めについてアドバイスする

steps.t: When do the stitches come out?

steps.cue: 抜糸の時期を説明する

steps.t: OK, thank you.

steps.cue: 理解を確認する

steps.t: Thank you. That's the end of the second role-play.

r1_1.q: Nurse, I'm not getting up today. My knee hurts too much.
r1_1.ja: 歩きたくない理由をたずねる
model: I'm sorry your knee is hurting. Can you tell me a bit more about how you're feeling? Is it mainly the pain, or are you worried about something else?
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_2.q: Well, both. I'm afraid I'll fall and damage the new knee.
r1_2.ja: 痛みと不安を受けとめる
model: That's a very understandable worry, and lots of patients feel the same way. Thank you for telling me.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_3.q: So why can't I just stay in bed for a few days?
r1_3.ja: 早く歩くことの大切さを説明する(血栓・回復)
model: Staying in bed for too long can actually slow down your recovery. Getting up early helps prevent blood clots, keeps your muscles strong and helps the new knee move better.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_4.ja: 安全に歩くための支えを説明する(痛み止め・歩行器・付き添い)
model: I'll make sure you're safe. We'll give you some pain relief first, and then I'll be right beside you with a walking frame. We'll only take a few steps to start with.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_5.q: Hmm, OK. Maybe I can try.
r1_5.ja: 計画に合意する(30分後に)
model: That's great. How about I bring your pain relief now, and we try in about thirty minutes, once it's working? We'll go at your pace.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_1.q: So I can go home now? What do I need to do with this bandage?
r2_1.ja: 傷の手当ての方法を説明する(乾かす)
model: Yes, you can go home today. Please keep the bandage clean and dry for the next five days. When you shower, cover your hand with a plastic bag.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_2.ja: 感染のサインを説明する
model: Good question. Please look out for signs of infection, like increasing redness, swelling, a bad smell, or if you develop a fever. If you notice any of these, call us straight away.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_3.q: It's starting to hurt a little.
r2_3.ja: 痛み止めについてアドバイスする
model: That's normal after the anaesthetic wears off. You can take paracetamol every six hours as needed, and keeping your hand raised on a pillow will also reduce the swelling.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_4.q: When do the stitches come out?
r2_4.ja: 抜糸の時期を説明する
model: The stitches will be removed in ten days. You can make an appointment with the practice nurse at your local clinic.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

model: You're welcome. Just to make sure I've explained everything clearly, could you tell me what signs would mean you need to call us?
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

roles.title: Role-play 1 (Medicine)
lines: Patient: a 25-year-old university student with a cold who is asking for antibiotics.
task: Find out about the patient's symptoms.
Explain that the illness is caused by a virus.
Explain why antibiotics will not help.
Suggest ways to relieve the symptoms.
Explain when to come back.

roles.title: Role-play 2 (Medicine)
lines: Patient: a 52-year-old taxi driver who has just been told he has type 2 diabetes.
task: Find out what the patient knows about diabetes.
Explain the condition simply.
Discuss diet and exercise.
Respond to the patient's concern about his job.
Explain the follow-up plan.

steps.t: So what can I do? I really need to study.

steps.cue: 症状を楽にする方法を提案する

steps.t: OK. And if it doesn't get better?

steps.cue: いつ再受診すべきか説明する

steps.t: Thank you. That's the end of the first role-play.

Diabetes? I don't really understand what that means.

steps.cue: 患者が知っていることをたずねる

steps.t: Only that it's something about sugar.

steps.cue: 病気をわかりやすく説明する

r1_1.q: Hi, doctor. I've got a terrible cold and I need antibiotics. I have exams next week.
r1_1.ja: 症状をたずねる(いつから・熱)
model: I'm sorry you're feeling unwell, especially before your exams. Can you tell me about your symptoms? When did they start, and have you had a fever?
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_2.q: Three days ago. Sore throat, runny nose, a bit of a temperature yesterday.
r1_2.ja: ウイルス性の風邪だと説明する
model: Thank you. From your symptoms and my examination, this looks like a common cold, which is caused by a virus.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_3.q: But antibiotics will make it go away faster, won't they?
r1_3.ja: 抗生物質が効かない理由を説明する
model: I can see why you'd think that, but antibiotics only work against bacteria, not viruses. They wouldn't help you get better faster, and they can cause side effects like stomach upset.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_4.q: So what can I do? I really need to study.
r1_4.ja: 症状を楽にする方法を提案する
model: Rest as much as you can, drink plenty of fluids, and you can take paracetamol for the sore throat and temperature. Most colds get better within a week to ten days.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r1_5.q: OK. And if it doesn't get better?
r1_5.ja: いつ再受診すべきか説明する
model: If you're not improving after ten days, or if you develop a high fever or difficulty breathing, please come back and we'll take another look. I hope your exams go well.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_1.q: Diabetes? I don't really understand what that means.
r2_1.ja: 患者が知っていることをたずねる
model: That's completely fine; it's a lot to take in. Before I explain, can I ask what you already know about diabetes, if anything?
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_2.q: Only that it's something about sugar.
r2_2.ja: 病気をわかりやすく説明する
model: You're right, it's about sugar. Your body isn't using insulin properly, so the sugar level in your blood is higher than it should be. Over time, that can damage your eyes, kidneys and heart, which is why we want to control it.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_3.q: Will I have to stop eating everything I like?
r2_3.ja: 食事と運動について話す
model: Not everything. It's more about balance: smaller portions, less sugary drinks and white rice, and more vegetables. Walking for thirty minutes a day would also make a big difference.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_4.q: I drive a taxi all day. How can I exercise?
r2_4.ja: 仕事についての心配に答える
model: I understand; long hours in the car make it hard. Perhaps you could take a short walk during your breaks, or park a little further away and walk. Even small changes help.
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

r2_5.ja: 今後の計画を説明する
model: We'll start you on a tablet called metformin, and you'll see a dietitian next week. We'll check your blood sugar again in three months. Do you have any questions so far?
points: 相手の言葉を受けとめてから(I understand …)
専門用語は言いかえる
確認の質問(Does that make sense?)

oet_wu.ja: どこで研修を受けましたか。
model: I trained at a university hospital in Tokyo, and I have been working there for three years.
points: 仕事の経歴を簡単に

oet_wu.q: What do you enjoy most about your work?
oet_wu.ja: 仕事でいちばん楽しいことは何ですか。
model: I enjoy seeing patients recover and go home. It makes the long shifts worthwhile.
points: 理由を一言

oet_wu.q: Why would you like to work abroad?
oet_wu.ja: なぜ海外で働きたいのですか。
model: I would like to learn about different healthcare systems and improve my skills in an international team.
points: 具体的に

oet_wu.q: What is a typical day like for you at work?
oet_wu.ja: 仕事の典型的な1日を教えてください。
model: I usually start at eight with a handover, then see patients on the ward and update their records.
points: 順番に
